GIG DRIVER EARNINGS REPORT ANALYZER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

What do you really earn per hour driving, after the car?

Drop in a trip or delivery history CSV and get net pay per hour and per mile after vehicle cost, which app, weekday and time of day pays best, and the trips that paid less than they cost to drive, without handing a mileage or earnings app access to your driver accounts.

The file is read in this browser tab and never leaves your device. Independent of Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, Instacart, Grubhub and every other app: not affiliated with or endorsed by any of them.

1. Your trip history

Export from your driver app, a mileage app such as Gridwise or Everlance, or keep a sheet. Needs a Date (with a time for time-of-day results) and Earnings (or Fare, Pay, Total); Tip, Miles (or Distance), Minutes (or Duration, or Start and End times) and Platform are used when present. US and day-first dates, comma, tab and semicolon files, and UTF-16 exports are read. Rows that cannot be read are listed with a line number and reason.

The default 0.70 is the IRS 2025 business mileage rate in dollars per mile; the rate is reset most years, so enter the current one or your own real cost.

Choose a file or paste the text, then click Analyze.

The model, and what it leaves out

  • Income is earnings plus tip on each row (or the Total column minus the tip if there is no earnings column). Rows are trips or deliveries; total rows are skipped.
  • Reconciles. The per-app, per-weekday and per-time rows each add up to the totals at the top.
  • Vehicle cost is the miles on each trip, plus the extra-mile percentage you enter, times your cost per mile. Trips with no miles are charged nothing, and the page says how many.
  • Net is income minus vehicle cost. Nothing else is subtracted.
  • Per hour uses trip minutes, which exclude waiting between trips, unless you enter your total hours online for the period, which then drives the headline figure. Per-group rates use only trips that report minutes.
  • Time of day and weekday are read from the file's own clock; no time zone conversion is applied. Groups with fewer than five trips are not ranked.
  • Not modelled: taxes, phone, insurance and tolls beyond your cost per mile, trips you declined or were never offered, incentives paid separately, and anything not in the file.

Common questions

How do I find out what I really earn per hour driving for Uber, Lyft or DoorDash?

Export your trip or delivery history from the app (or keep a sheet with a date, earnings, tip, miles and minutes) and drop it here. The tool adds each trip's pay and tip, subtracts your cost per mile times the miles you drove, and divides by the hours. If you enter your total hours online it uses those, so waiting time between trips is counted. Nothing is uploaded; the file is read in your browser.

What cost per mile should I use?

Use your own number. The IRS standard mileage rate for business use was 70 cents per mile for 2025 and is reset most years, so check the current figure; it is a rate meant to cover gas, wear, depreciation and insurance. Your real cost may be lower in a hybrid or higher in an older truck. The tool applies whatever you enter and shows how much of your pay it takes.

Which platform, weekday and time of day pays best?

The tool groups your trips by app, weekday and time of day and shows net pay per trip hour and per mile for each group with at least five trips. Trip hours leave out waiting between trips, and busy hours often have more waiting, so use the ranking to decide what to test next rather than as proof.

What does it not know?

Time spent online with no trip, unpaid miles to reach a pickup (unless you add a percentage for them), taxes, phone and insurance costs beyond your cost per mile, and anything not in your file. It cannot see surge you declined or trips you were not offered.

Is this tax or financial advice?

No. It applies arithmetic to the file you provide and does not replace your own judgement or a qualified tax adviser. It is independent of Uber, Lyft, DoorDash and every other app and is not affiliated with or endorsed by any of them.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record — nothing you enter is saved anywhere by this tool.

Everything runs in your browser. Your file is never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (csv_analyzed, example_loaded) are counted only in local storage on your device. The counts can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.
